independent_retrievals.title: HTTP Semantics
independent_retrievals.verified_support: Byte-offset conditional retrieval is a real recovery mechanism. If-Range has validator-strength prerequisites; response metadata and representation scope matter.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: Service support, globally unique ETags across refreshed URLs, filesystem publication or a manifest API.

independent_retrievals.title: Digest Fields

locators.section: B.3: partial response with both digests

independent_retrievals.verified_support: Message content and complete selected representation have different digest scopes. Requesting a digest is advisory. RFC 3230 and its old fields are superseded.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: Mandatory service digest support, authenticated artifact manifests, name resolution or content-addressed storage APIs.

independent_retrievals.title: Metalink Download Description Format

locators.section: 4.1.3: ordered pieces, algorithm and octet length

independent_retrievals.verified_support: Mirror descriptions and ordered piece hashes enable selective repair. The format supports the proposed B ingredients; runtime journaling and promotion are client policy.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: That every manifest includes piece hashes, that metadata is trustworthy by presence alone, or that aria2 performs both integrity gates by default.

independent_retrievals.title: CURLOPT_RESUME_FROM
independent_retrievals.version: Live API page retrieved 2026-10-10; option introduced in curl 7.1; Last-Modified 2026-09-06
independent_retrievals.verified_support: The option takes a long byte offset, defaults to zero, has FTP-specific -1 behavior, and directs offsets beyond 2 GB to the LARGE option. HTTP POST/PUT resume is rejected.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: Automatic artifact identity validation, If-Range setup, checksum gating or atomic finalization.

independent_retrievals.title: Resumable upload protocol
independent_retrievals.verified_support: Upload receiver owns the upload offset; HEAD reports it and PATCH advances it. Optional checksum extension validates incoming request chunks and leaves the offset unchanged on rejection.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: Download receiver durable state, a download acknowledgment protocol, download checksums or signed-download session reissue.

independent_retrievals.title: aria2c manual

locators.section: Description: multi-source downloads and chunk validation

independent_retrievals.verified_support: The aria2 implementation lead is substantive: multi-source transfers, chunk validation and selective re-download are documented. Integrity-check default and piece-versus-whole selection need explicit attention.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: That the candidate inspected source code or that the proposed second whole-file check follows automatically from default aria2 behavior.

independent_retrievals.title: curl manual
independent_retrievals.version: The retrieved page declares curl 8.23.0; live documentation, not a tested installed client
independent_retrievals.verified_support: -C - derives an offset from input/output files; the documented operation is byte continuation.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: Remote identity, hash verification or which version the candidate used.

independent_retrievals.title: rename / renameat
independent_retrievals.verified_support: POSIX atomic namespace replacement is a valid conditional basis for publication; cross-filesystem failures are relevant.
independent_retrievals.does_not_establish: All desktop operating-system behavior, crash durability or service behavior.

finding_evidence.judgment: The cited protocol establishes upload-receiver progress, not durable bytes at a download receiver. The adaptation lacks the consequential receiver-persistence/acknowledgment invariant and does not investigate it.

The date-validator prerequisites are missing: HTTP-date If-Range is restricted to the absence of an entity tag and a date that qualifies as strong. A stored Last-Modified value alone does not meet that condition.

A/B/C offer distinct recovery/identity variants; overlap is allowed by the brief. D does not investigate the direction/persistence condition. No automatic winner; qualitative cost estimates not measured. Prior familiarity is unknown.
All required lead slots exist; curl and aria2 are real leads and current/older standards are useful history leads. Four-item applicability shortfall is substantive, not a count failure.
Governing primary text independently retrieved; F1 and F2 remain material. Conditions C01-C10 distinguish source operations from proposed composition.

Range ignorance, identity replacement, URL expiry, piece repair and finalization are explored. The fourth applicable mechanism and date-validator boundary remain missing. Integrity-failure wording is an open question; a finished UI is not required.

conditions.candidate_coverage: Weak ETag boundary is mentioned; HTTP-date prerequisites are not.

conditions.status: covered at discovery level with implementation detail unresolved
conditions.candidate_coverage: Ignored Range/full 200, matching 206 and stale If-Range are recognized. Matching must include response range interpretation; 206 Content-Length is not necessarily artifact total. Accept-Ranges is advisory; offset-at-end/416 may require a local integrity check rather than restart inference.

Fresh URL resolution is proposed; endpoint/lifetime unknown. A validator is not globally unique across distinct resources; same-byte identity through URL replacement must come from artifact metadata or a defined service contract. The brief does not require a particular service already to exist.

conditions.status: useful sources; detailed field/coding operation unresolved
conditions.candidate_coverage: A explicitly proposes a manifest whole-file gate, so it is not credited as verifying the assembled artifact from a partial response Content-Digest. Content-Digest and Repr-Digest have different subjects; coding transformations matter. A digest preference request can be ignored. Metadata/hash service and acceptable algorithms remain unobserved.

conditions.topic: Metalink fields, algorithm, piece geometry and trust
conditions.status: mechanism supported; some boundaries omitted nonmaterially for this brief
conditions.candidate_coverage: The proposed manifest contains piece and whole-file hashes; such fields are not mandatory in every Metalink. Piece ordering, octet length and final-piece exception govern verification. SHA-256 support is specified by RFC 5854; source metadata trust still matters.

conditions.topic: aria2 behavior versus proposed dual integrity gate
conditions.status: lead supported, automatic equivalence not established
conditions.candidate_coverage: aria2 1.37.0 documents realtime chunk checks by default, --check-integrity=false by default, and piece-hash precedence when both forms are present. The candidate proposes its own whole-file promotion gate; no claim of a tested default aria2 dual gate is credited.

Byte offsets, long versus curl_off_t, zero default, beyond-2-GB note and -C - behavior are corroborated. FTP -1 and HTTP POST/PUT restrictions are source-specific; this brief is downloads. The resume option alone is not credited as an identity gate.

conditions.topic: tus direction and receiver durable offset
conditions.candidate_coverage: The candidate correctly labels uploads and optional extension/expiry limits, but does not establish a usable durable download offset. Server session ownership cannot substitute for evidence of locally persisted bytes.

Temporary destination, pre-publication whole-file check and rename are useful. Application kill and power-loss durability are different checks; fsync error handling/directory persistence and cross-platform semantics are not observations. The candidate explicitly leaves rename guarantees unknown.
RFC 9110 / 7233 and RFC 9530 / 3230 replacements are supported, as is a reason to revisit old examples. Not every historical change is a tightening.

limitations.description: The curl and aria2 leads are real and inspectable, but the candidate does not pin an upstream revision or report source-code inspection. The assessor corroborated public project documentation only; repository-code inspection remains unknown.

The statements that B pays off only for large files on flaky links and that C alone makes replacement explicit overstate the evidence. B has other possible concurrency/mirror benefits; the candidate table already gives replacement responses for A and B. No winner is declared, so these are comparison limitations rather than an independently material selection error.

Final publication is expressly a proposed composition. Atomic-rename support and crash recovery are left for investigation. POSIX rename and Linux fsync illustrate why namespace atomicity, cross-filesystem behavior and directory durability must be separated; no desktop/platform durability guarantee is demonstrated.

Saved source files are short factual summaries, mostly abstracts/table-of-contents material; S1 explicitly cites supporting search results for If-Range. They do not demonstrate all consequential section reads or the complete candidate retrieval count. Independently retrieved governing text, not these summaries or matching hashes, grounds this source judgment.

The three named probes have meaningful observables, but they do not directly compare piece repair with whole-file retry, exercise D receiver-durable progress, or deliberately inject corruption to check integrity-failure behavior. They remain proposals, not observed successes. The D persistence gap is already material F1.

The standards replacement dates and a useful historical comparison are supported. Exact-match language was already present in RFC 7233, and RFC 9110 relaxed a Last-Modified age rule, so hardened along the way is a loose historical summary rather than a precise version change.
